$schema_note: Generated by tools/uesp/mine-argonian-names.mjs from the UESP extract. Hand verdicts in gloss_conflicts and phonotactic_validation.interpretation ARE editorial.

source.provenance: community-data for every name and gloss; derived for classification, counts and verdicts
source.era_note: ESO names are 2E 582; Morrowind/Tribunal/Bloodmoon names are 3E 427 — the era of our game. Where the two disagree about naming FASHION, the Morrowind-era set is the one to imitate.

phonotactic_validation.question: RI-LOR04 asks whether the constructed Jel phonotactics in jel-lexicon.json actually match real Argonian naming. This runs the corpus's own validator against the words Bethesda and ZOS actually shipped.
rejected_attested_words: Greel [jel] [Greel] forbidden cluster 'gr'; [Greel] illegal initial cluster 'gr'
interpretation: THE CONSTRUCTED PHONOTACTICS REJECT REAL JEL. 26.7% of attested Jel words fail a validator whose own pass threshold is 5%.

The rejections are not edge cases. Saxhleel — the Argonians' word for themselves — is rejected for the medial cluster "xhl". Thtithil (egg), which the corpus already cites as canon in CF-025, is rejected for the initial cluster "tht". Xeech (seed), a root our own lexicon lists, is rejected for the final cluster "ch".
Two of the failures are our forbidden-cluster list being stricter than canon: greel (enemy) uses "gr" and krona (big) uses "kr", both banned outright as "epic-fantasy" clusters. Canon Jel has them.
One is our no-geminates rule: vakka (sun) has "kk". The rule exists for good reasons and it is wrong.

This does NOT mean the phonology is bad design — a constructed dialect may legitimately be narrower than the attested corpus. It means the validator is currently calibrated to fail canon, which is the opposite of what a canon-fidelity tool should do. Either the attested words go into attested_exceptions (they are, after all, attested), or the cluster and geminate rules are relaxed to admit them. Doing neither ships a validator that would reject an Argonian saying their own name for their own people.

gloss_conflicts.method: Every root in jel-lexicon.json that also appears in an attested source, compared by hand.

entries.attested_gloss: Death, or pertaining to death. Also known as rebirth, for they are thought to be one and the same in the eyes of my people.
entries.attested_source: Lore:The Sharper Tongue: A Jel Primer
entries.note: The primer glosses xul as "Death, or pertaining to death. Also known as rebirth, for they are thought to be one and the same." Our lexicon has xul = "root, that which goes down" (marked `inferred`). Every coined term built on it — xul-teekh (souls), ixtu-xul (sapwell), xul-vaska, xul-hesh, xul-aneekh (the Deep-Kin) — therefore reads to a Jel speaker as death-X, not root-X. For xul-teekh (soul-residue of a death) and xul-hesh (soul-trapping) this is a lucky improvement. For xul-aneekh ("Deep-Kin") it is wrong: it reads as "Death-Kin".

entries.our_gloss: friend, one bound to you by water
entries.attested_gloss: Friend. Variations include: Deek-Beeko, Raj-Beeko, Beek-Ojel, and Uxith-Beeko.
entries.attested_source: Lore:The Sharper Tongue: A Jel Primer
entries.note: Primer: "Beeko: Friend." Our added gloss "one bound to you by water" is ours, not the source's. The primer does give real compounds: Deek-Beeko, Raj-Beeko, Beek-Ojel, Uxith-Beeko.

entries.attested_gloss: Teacher, or more accurately, one who passes wisdom to another. A very honored title for any to be granted.
entries.attested_source: Lore:The Sharper Tongue: A Jel Primer
entries.note: Primer: "Deelith: Teacher, or more accurately, one who passes wisdom to another." Matches.

entries.our_gloss: change; ku-vastei = the change that is owed
entries.attested_gloss: Change. Perhaps the greatest driving force behind my people's motivation. To go against change is known to be the greatest folly.
entries.attested_source: Lore:The Sharper Tongue: A Jel Primer
entries.note: Primer: "Vastei: Change. Perhaps the greatest driving force behind my people's motivation." Matches.

entries.our_gloss: salted one; an Argonian assimilated to foreign ways
entries.attested_gloss: An Argonian that has assimilated into a non-Argonian culture. They are often treated as outsiders by the natives of Black Marsh.
entries.attested_source: Lore:The Sharper Tongue: A Jel Primer
entries.note: Primer: "Lukiul: An Argonian that has assimilated into a non-Argonian culture." Our gloss adds "salted one", which is ours.

entries.attested_gloss: Hides, hidden. It's easy to see why it is part of the creature haj mota's name.
entries.attested_source: Lore:The Sharper Tongue: A Jel Primer
entries.note: Primer: "Haj: Hides, hidden. It's easy to see why it is part of the creature haj mota's name." This also confirms the corpus's decomposition of haj mota.

entries.attested_gloss: Nut, seed. Also the beginning, birth, something with unreleased potential.
entries.attested_source: Lore:The Sharper Tongue: A Jel Primer
entries.note: Primer: "Xeech: Nut, seed. Also the beginning, birth, something with unreleased potential." Our gloss is just "seed"; the attested word already carries the metaphor the corpus was going to have to invent.

entries.our_gloss: tongue, the organ; by extension a manner of speaking
entries.attested_gloss: Not of a tribe, outsider. Literally meaning, "Not of Argonian Tongue" or perhaps "Non-Speaker of Jel."
entries.attested_source: Lore:The Sharper Tongue: A Jel Primer
entries.note: The primer glosses ojel as "Not of a tribe, outsider. Literally, Not of Argonian Tongue." Our lexicon has ojel = "tongue, the organ" (`inferred`). The morphology our entry guesses at (o- + jel) is right; the gloss is not. Ojel is the Argonian word for a foreigner, which is far more useful than "tongue" and should replace it.

entries.attested_gloss: Nest, home, bed. For my people, these concepts are one in the same. Be wary if you are asked to become someone's uxith-beeko.
entries.attested_source: Lore:The Sharper Tongue: A Jel Primer
entries.note: The primer glosses uxith as "Nest, home, bed. For my people, these concepts are one in the same." Our lexicon has uxith = "old, long-standing, kept" AND marks it `community-data`, i.e. claims a source. It does not have one. This is the clearest case in the corpus of recall being logged as sourced.

entries.our_gloss: to kneel, to put the hand down into
entries.attested_gloss: War captain. The more violent the tribe, the more this title is revered.
entries.attested_source: Lore:The Sharper Tongue: A Jel Primer
entries.note: The primer glosses kaal as "War captain. The more violent the tribe, the more this title is revered." Our lexicon coins kaal = "to kneel, to put the hand down into" as `constructed`. A constructed root has landed on an attested one with an unrelated meaning. Rename ours.

naming_grammar_as_attested.note: RI-LOR04 legislates "[Verb-3sg] - [optional Determiner|Possessive] - [Noun], 2-4 words, modal 3" for Tamrielic Argonian names. This is what the shipped games actually do.
naming_grammar_as_attested.classifier_note: shape is DERIVED by a declared heuristic: a hyphen/space component counts as Tamrielic if it is in an English word list fitted to this corpus; a majority-English name is tamrielic-descriptive, otherwise jel-compound. Names carrying an attested Argonian title prefix (Tree-Minder, Nisswo, Raj-Kaal, Sap-Speaker…) have the title stripped before classification.
